identification.summary: Trend Micro describes Earth Freybug as a cyberthreat group active since at least 2012 that conducts espionage and financially motivated activity, and as a subset of APT41 [S2]. Trend Micro's 2 April 2024 report described a campaign in which the group used DLL hijacking and API unhooking through a previously undocumented malware it named UNAPIMON [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: Trend Micro: active since at least 2012 [S2]. The UNAPIMON campaign was reported 2024-04-02 [S3].
identification.notes: Earth Freybug is a Trend Micro cluster name. Trend Micro says its TTPs are similar to the activity Cybereason reported as Operation CuckooBees [S2]. Secondary coverage lists APT41 aliases such as Winnti, Wicked Panda, Brass Typhoon (formerly Barium), Axiom, Bronze Atlas and HOODOO [S2][S4]. These are aliases of the broader APT41 set, not of Earth Freybug, so none were added here.

attribution.confidence: Trend Micro characterizes Earth Freybug as a subset of APT41, a China-linked group [S2][S4]. RH-ISAC's write-up states the report matched TTPs of Operation CuckooBees, which it describes as widely attributed to Winnti/APT41 [S3]. No government attribution of Earth Freybug specifically was found.
attribution.basis: Trend Micro TTP comparison with Operation CuckooBees [S3]; vendor characterization as an APT41 subset [S2].

objectives: Trend Micro describes the group as focused on espionage and financially motivated activity [S2]. Specific collection requirements in the UNAPIMON campaign are not stated in the sources reviewed.

targeting.notes: Trend Micro says the group attacks organizations across various sectors and countries; the sources reviewed did not name specific sectors, countries or victims for the UNAPIMON campaign [S3].

capabilities.summary: Trend Micro reports use of living-off-the-land binaries together with custom malware, plus DLL hijacking and API unhooking [S2][S3]. In the observed chain a process in the legitimate VMware Tools binary vmtoolsd.exe used schtasks.exe to create a remote scheduled task that ran a pre-deployed batch file (cc.bat) for reconnaissance and to launch further tasks [S2]. A later batch step reportedly side-loaded a DLL (TSMSISrv.dll) via the SessionEnv service to load UNAPIMON into a cmd.exe process [S5]. UNAPIMON is a C++ DLL, neither packed nor obfuscated, that uses Microsoft Detours to hook CreateProcessW and unhook API hooks in child processes, preventing security tools from monitoring them [S3][S5]. How the VMware Tools process was initially compromised is unknown; exploitation of external-facing servers is suspected [S2].

campaigns.summary: Trend Micro states the group has been active since at least 2012; no specific campaigns from that period are cited in the sources reviewed.

campaigns.name: UNAPIMON campaign
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro published analysis of an Earth Freybug intrusion using a vmtoolsd.exe process to create remote scheduled tasks running cc.bat, then DLL side-loading to deploy the UNAPIMON API-unhooking malware, with TTPs similar to Operation CuckooBees.

diamond.adversary: Cluster described by Trend Micro as an APT41 subset, China-linked, active since at least 2012 [S2][S4].
diamond.capability: LOLBins, custom malware (UNAPIMON), DLL hijacking/side-loading, Microsoft Detours-based API unhooking, scheduled tasks and batch scripts [S2][S5].
diamond.victim: Organizations across various sectors and countries; none named in sources reviewed [S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage and financially motivated activity per Trend Micro [S2].
diamond.technology: Windows hosts running VMware Tools (vmtoolsd.exe), Task Scheduler and the SessionEnv service; endpoint security that relies on API hooking [S5].

gaps: Trend Micro's primary report could not be fetched or confirmed in search results, so it is not cited; details rest on secondary coverage (The Hacker News, RH-ISAC, Dark Reading, BleepingComputer).
Victim sectors, countries and number of victims are not identified in the sources reviewed.
Initial access vector is unknown; exploitation of external-facing servers is only suspected [S2].
C2 infrastructure and indicators were not captured.
Only one dated campaign (April 2024) was found; no earlier Earth Freybug campaigns were located, and activity after April 2024 was not found.
Relationship to the rest of APT41 (and to Microsoft's Brass Typhoon naming) is a vendor characterization (subset); the cluster boundary is not independently verified.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID or Microsoft name mapping was found for Earth Freybug.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Virtualized Windows servers running VMware Tools and Task Scheduler are the relevant terrain [S5]. STEP 2: The group's defense-evasion approach (unhooking API monitoring in child processes) degrades hook-based EDR visibility on affected hosts [S3][S5]. STEP 3: Observed pattern is a trusted process (vmtoolsd.exe) creating remote scheduled tasks that run batch files, then DLL side-loading to load UNAPIMON [S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage-focused intrusion using LOLBins and custom tooling against organizations in multiple sectors [S2]. MDCOA, which is speculative as the sources do not show it, is the same unhooking capability applied to defense-sector networks to run follow-on tools unseen. Candidate indicators: vmtoolsd.exe spawning schtasks.exe or cmd.exe, creation of remote tasks running cc.bat, TSMSISrv.dll loaded via SessionEnv, and hooks on CreateProcessW added by Detours [S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: because EDR hook visibility can be blinded, supplement with kernel/ETW and process-lineage telemetry and track the Trend Micro and APT41 reporting [S3]. (2) Authorities: hunting on contractor or partner hosts requires the appropriate owner or DIB CS coordination; confirm authority before acting. (3) Mission assurance: apply least privilege and restrict admin accounts, as Trend Micro recommends, on virtualization and management hosts [S3]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with DC3 and partners, noting that victim and infrastructure data are unavailable and attribution is vendor-level only [S2].

provenance.importedSummary: Earth Freybug, identified as a subset of APT41, is a cyberthreat group active since at least 2012, engaging in espionage and financially motivated activities across various sectors worldwide. The tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) used in this campaign are similar to the ones from a campaign (Operation CuckooBees) described in an article published by Cybereason. They employ a diverse toolkit, including LOLBins and custom malware, to execute sophisticated cyberespionage attacks. The group's recent tactics involve DLL hijacking and API unhooking through a newly discovered malware named UNAPIMON, which prevents child processes from being monitored. This technique was observed in a vmtoolsd.exe process creating remote tasks to deploy malicious batch files for reconnaissance and backdoor access. UNAPIMON's simplicity and use of Microsoft Detours for defense evasion highlight the group's evolving methods and the need for vigilant security measures, such as restricting admin privileges and adhering to the principle of least privilege. Earth Freybug's persistence and creativity in refining their techniques underscore the ongoing threat they pose and the importance of proactive cybersecurity practices.
